sections.heading: Learning Point 1
sections.content: Electricity: Circuits and their Components 3 Nihal and his classmates were excited for their school trip to the Bhakra Nangal Dam.
sections.source_evidence: Electricity: Circuits and their Components 3 Nihal and his classmates were excited for their school trip to the Bhakra Nangal Dam.

sections.heading: Learning Point 2
sections.content: There they would visit the hydroelectric power house where the force of falling water was used to generate electricity.

sections.heading: Learning Point 3
sections.content: They also looked forward to the free 13 kilometre- train ride from Nangal in Punjab to Bhakra in Himachal Pradesh, along the beautiful Sutlej river and through the Shivalik hills.

sections.heading: Learning Point 4
sections.content: Prior to the trip, Nihal and his classmates were given a group assignment to prepare a presentation on the uses of electricity.

sections.content: They began by looking around their houses, then their school, followed by their neighbourhood, their city, and ﬁ nally they searched the internet.

sections.heading: Learning Point 11
sections.content: We use electricity all the time, so let us learn something more about electricity.

sections.heading: Learning Point 12
sections.content: You have learnt earlier that electricity is generated in multiple ways — by windmills, by using wind energy, by solar panels capturing the Sun’s energy, by falling water and by using natural gas or coal (in the chapter ‘Nature’s Treasures’ in the Grade 6 Science textbook Curiosity).

sections.heading: Learning Point 13
sections.content: The electric supply from these sources reaches our homes and factories via wires.

sections.heading: Learning Point 14
sections.content: For example, at home we plug in various devices to the electrical sockets in the wall.

sections.heading: Learning Point 15
sections.content: However, to learn about electricity, we will focus on a portable source of electricity that most of us may have used.

sections.heading: Learning Point 16
sections.content: Let us start with its use in a common device like a torchlight.

sections.heading: Learning Point 17
sections.content: Caution — The danger signs on electric poles and other appliances warn people that electricity can be dangerous if not carefully handled.

sections.heading: Learning Point 18
sections.content: Never ever perform experiments with power supply at your home or school.
sections.source_evidence: Never ever perform experiments with power supply at your home or school.

sections.heading: Learning Point 19
sections.content: Even electricity from portable generators can be dangerous.
sections.source_evidence: Even electricity from portable generators can be dangerous.

sections.heading: Learning Point 20
sections.content: Use only batteries or cells, like those in torchlights, wall clocks, radios, or remotes, for experiments with electricity.
